Container.Name: OpenScrub-Intel
Container.Overview:
Local video redaction with a human review step. OpenScrub scans videos and screen recordings for PII — faces, whole people (silhouette-precise body masking), license plates, and on-screen text such as names, phone numbers, SSNs, emails, addresses and card numbers, plus your own custom regex categories — then blurs, boxes or pixelates it. Every detection is shown as a thumbnail you approve or reject before the final render, and each run produces an audit report with input/output hashes. Spoken-PII detection can suggest audio mute spans from a local transcription. Nothing ever leaves your server.
This is the Intel build: hardware (Quick Sync) video encoding and OpenVINO-accelerated detection on any Intel iGPU (Gen 9+) or Arc card. Pass /dev/dri through (preconfigured below) to enable the GPU — without it everything still works on the CPU. The image ships Intel's media driver; the host needs no extra driver install.
First browser visit shows a certificate warning (self-signed TLS — footage stays private on your LAN); accept it to continue. Detection models download on first use and persist in appdata.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: redact redaction blur faces privacy PII anonymize license plate video scrub
Container.Requires: Optional: an Intel iGPU (Gen 9+) or Arc card for hardware encode/inference — pass /dev/dri (preconfigured). Works CPU-only without it. Internet access on first use to download detection models (persisted in appdata).

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: HTTPS port for the web interface (self-signed TLS by default).

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Persistent data: jobs, reports, downloaded detection models, settings, certificates.

Config.Name: Intel GPU
Config.Description: Intel GPU device for Quick Sync encoding and OpenVINO inference. Remove if the server has no Intel GPU — OpenScrub falls back to CPU automatically.
